false_positives.title: `lodash.template` release(template): bump to 4.18.1
false_positives.model_rationale: This release bump fixes a ReferenceError bug in the documented `_.template` function, meaning a documented feature that was broken for valid usage now works — a real user-facing change (see rule 1). The change swaps `assignInWith`/`keysIn` internals for `assignWith`/`keys` to resolve the crash, though the public `_.template` signature is unchanged.
false_positives.label_rationale: Restores an internal helper (arrayEach) that had been dropped from the lodash.template standalone bundle, fixing packaging/bundling correctness. arrayEach/baseKeysIn are private implementation details, not part of the documented public API.

false_negatives.title: Make z.preprocess defer optionality to inner schema
false_negatives.label_rationale: Introduces a new exported ZodPreprocess class and changes how z.preprocess()'s optionality is inferred from the inner schema. The PR itself edits packages/docs/content/packages/core.mdx, confirming it's a documented public API change.

false_negatives.title: fix(v4): reject tuple holes before required defaults
false_negatives.label_rationale: Changes z.tuple()'s runtime parse behavior: an absent optional slot before a later required/defaulted output slot now correctly fails instead of silently truncating and materializing the default. This flips success/failure for real inputs against the documented tuple API.

rows.title: feat(HttpStatusCode): add missing 520 status code
rows.model_rationale: Adds a new public enum member `HttpStatusCode.WebServerReturnsAnUnknownError = 520` to the runtime API and TypeScript declarations. The PR itself updates the changelog and requests a docs update for the status code reference, confirming user-facing relevance.
rows.label_rationale: Adds a new exported constant (HttpStatusCode.WebServerReturnsAnUnknownError = 520) across ESM/CJS type declarations and the runtime object — a new public API member that any status-code reference docs would need to list.

rows.title: fix(core): synchronous interceptors swallow errors and proceed with request
rows.model_rationale: This changes the observable behavior of documented synchronous request interceptors: thrown errors no longer dispatch the request unless the paired onRejected resolves, and terminal errors now flow to response rejection interceptors. The in-PR changelog and docs-planning notes explicitly flag the Interceptors section, README, and API reference as needing updates, confirming user-facing relevance.
rows.label_rationale: Changes the documented contract for synchronous request interceptor error handling (paired onRejected semantics, when the request dispatches vs. rejects). PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md is updated in the same diff with the exact behavior to document.

rows.title: feat(types): Allow the Params property to be typed, instead of `any`
rows.model_rationale: This adds a new public generic parameter `P` to `AxiosRequestConfig` and propagates typed params across the public TypeScript surface (`AxiosResponse`, `AxiosError`, `CanceledError`, `isCancel`, `mergeConfig`, request aliases, `AxiosPromise`, serializers). The PR itself updates the changelog and pre-release docs plan, confirming it's a user-facing typing change worth documenting.
rows.label_rationale: Adds a second generic parameter to AxiosRequestConfig/AxiosPromise/isCancel and propagates it through public type declarations (index.d.ts/index.d.cts). The PR itself edits PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md with usage examples, confirming the maintainers consider this a documented public API surface change.

rows.title: fix(core): synthesize AxiosError message from AggregateError.errors
rows.model_rationale: AxiosError.from() now synthesizes a message from AggregateError.errors when the outer message is blank, changing the observable message/toJSON output for a documented error type on network failures. The PR also updated the changelog, confirming maintainers view it as user-facing.
rows.label_rationale: AxiosError.from() now synthesizes a .message from AggregateError.errors instead of leaving it blank, and toJSON() carries it. The PR updates PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md in the same diff, confirming the maintainers consider this a user-facing change worth describing.

rows.title: fix(helpers): correct data: URL base64 size estimate for maxContentLength guard
rows.model_rationale: This is a behavior fix that changes how the documented maxContentLength guard is enforced for data: URLs: bodies that previously bypassed the limit (up to ~2x maxContentLength) are now correctly rejected, and fetch now ignores URL fragments in the size estimate. The PR also adds a changelog entry, confirming maintainer intent to describe it to users. The estimateDataURLDecodedBytes helper appears internal, but the observable maxContentLength behavior is user-facing.
rows.label_rationale: Fixes how the documented maxContentLength option is enforced for data: URLs — previously percent-encoded input could bypass the configured limit. This changes observable behavior of a documented config option.

rows.title: refactor(helpers): extract duplicated setFormDataHeaders into a shared helper
rows.model_rationale: Though framed as a refactor, the extraction adopts the defensive `formHeaders || {}` variant in the http adapter, so Node.js requests with `formDataHeaderPolicy: 'content-only'` now tolerate a FormData implementation whose `getHeaders()` returns undefined instead of throwing. This is a real user-facing behavior fix for a documented option, confirmed by the PR's own changelog entry.
rows.label_rationale: Framed as a refactor, but the extracted helper also fixes a real bug: with formDataHeaderPolicy: 'content-only', a custom FormData#getHeaders() that returns undefined used to throw, now it's tolerated. This is a behavior fix for a documented config option, not just a refactor.

rows.title: Tighten discriminated union option typing
rows.model_rationale: This is a compile-time TypeScript typing tightening for discriminatedUnion — options must now include the discriminator key in their input type, enforced via generic constraints. Runtime behavior is unchanged (the invalid case already threw), and the change only adds a stricter type-level error. Zod docs describe discriminatedUnion usage generally without specifying this constraint detail, so it's a niche compile-time refinement unlikely to warrant a public docs update; leaning false but with some uncertainty.
rows.label_rationale: Narrows a TypeScript generic constraint so z.discriminatedUnion() rejects, at compile time, an object option that's missing the discriminator key — a rare misuse case. No runtime behavior changes and normal documented usage is unaffected.

rows.title: fix(v4): skip __proto__ key in object catchall
rows.model_rationale: This is a security fix that changes how documented object methods (passthrough, catchall, looseObject) handle input containing a __proto__ key — previously such input polluted the parsed result's prototype, now it is skipped. This matches the worked example of the prior __proto__ catchall fix and warrants a changelog/security note.
rows.label_rationale: Security fix closing a prototype-pollution vector in .passthrough()/.catchall()/looseObject() (linked GitHub security advisories). This changes documented-schema parsing behavior for a security-sensitive input and warrants a docs/changelog note.

rows.title: fix(v4): generalize optin/fallback to transform; restore preprocess on absent keys
rows.model_rationale: This changes observable behavior of documented Zod v4 primitives: preprocess now accepts absent object keys again (restoring 4.3 parity), standalone z.transform now accepts absent object keys, and catch()/transform()/optional() chains now clobber recovery values through pipe boundaries (e.g. output changed from "X!" to undefined). These are real user-facing behavior changes to documented APIs, warranting a changelog/docs note. The wiki doc is internal-only, but the source-level behavior changes drive relevance.
rows.label_rationale: Changes how .optional() interacts with .catch()/.transform()/.preprocess() across pipe boundaries on absent input — a documented schema-composition behavior that previously produced wrong results (e.g. transform output leaking through an outer .optional()).

rows.title: Various tweaks
rows.model_rationale: Despite the modest "Various tweaks" title, the diff is a security-relevant behavior change: when a beforeRequest/afterResponse/pagination hook rewrites `prefixUrl` to a cross-origin target, Got now strips sensitive headers (authorization, cookie), inherited credentials, and the request body — mirroring existing cross-origin URL protections. It also changes credential-inheritance behavior for prefixUrl changes. This alters what documented options (prefixUrl, credentials, cross-origin header stripping) do for real users and warrants a docs/changelog note.
rows.label_rationale: Changes cross-origin redirect handling: which sensitive headers get stripped and when the request body is discarded/preserved after a beforeRequest hook changes the URL to a different origin. This is documented redirect/security behavior (see the cross-origin stripping notes in 2-options.md) being corrected.
